title: When Faith Has Questions
subtitle: For the reader taking the faith apart — four essays, a study, and a book.
forWhom: For the Christian with real questions and the skeptic who left over them — anyone who would rather have an honest doubt than a dishonest certainty.

movements.heading: Read these first
movements.note: Take the hardest questions at full strength before any answer — deconstruction, the hiddenness of God, suffering, and the one claim the whole thing stands or falls on.

items.label: What Happens After You Deconstruct Your Faith?
items.blurb: Taking a faith apart is honest work. Stopping there is just standing in the rubble.

items.label: Why Does God Hide?
items.blurb: The silence is not proof of absence. But it is not nothing, and Scripture never pretends it is.

items.label: Why Does God Allow Suffering?
items.blurb: The oldest objection, taken at its strongest, without the tidy answer that insults the wound.

items.label: Did the Resurrection Actually Happen?
items.blurb: The one question under all the others. If it is yes, everything else can be carried.

movements.heading: Then work the study
movements.note: When Faith Has Questions is a five-session study — suffering, the reliability of Scripture, the wounds of the church — every hard question named before it is answered. A safe room for the doubter.

items.label: When Faith Has Questions — a study on doubt
items.blurb: Five sessions for skeptics, questioners, and the groups brave enough to host them.

movements.heading: Then read the book, free
movements.note: Born Again From Atheism is the whole account of a man who left unbelief slowly, against his preference, and did not trade it for a god that small. Read it free; buy the ebook if it is worth keeping.

items.label: Born Again From Atheism — read free
items.blurb: Twelve chapters, written toward the reader still on the other side. The complete book, free to read.

items.label: Read a sample and buy the ebook
items.blurb: The book's own page, with a free excerpt and the purchase.
